properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 10 at 3:49PM MST until August 10 at 7:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The North and South Canyon Wash Basins downstream of the Dragon
Bravo Fire scar in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 700 PM MST /800 PM MDT/.

* At 349 PM MST /449 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the North and South Canyon Wash Basin
downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar. Between 1.5 and 2.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to
0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the North and South Canyon
Wash Basins downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
North and South Canyon Wash Basins downstream of the
Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Saddle Mountain Wilderness, Triple Alcoves, Royal Arches, Bert
Loper's Boat, Point Hansbrough, North Rim Entrance Station and
Anasazi Foot Bridge.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 67 between mile markers 609 and 610. the Colorado River
near river mile 32...and between river miles 37 and 43...and between
river miles 45 and 47.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
North Canyon, South Canyon, Buck Farm Canyon, House Rock Wash,
Colorado River, Tatahatso Wash and Saddle Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Flash flooding is occurring or imminent downstream of the Dragon
Bravo Fire scar. Severe debris flow are expected across roads and in
remote canyon drainages on the Kaibab Plateau east of State Route 67.
Campers and hikers should get away from creeks and move to higher
ground immediately! Stay away or be swept away!

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 10 at 5:50PM MDT until August 10 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Cottonwood burn scar in...
East Central Beaver County in southern Utah...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 550 PM MDT, Peak flows have already occurred in Beaver Canyon,
but flows will remain high in the Grove area before gradually
receding over the next hour. We are monitoring additional
thunderstorms in the area at this time. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Cottonwood Burn Scar in
Beaver county.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Cottonwood Burn Scar in Beaver County.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Beaver County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Cottonwood Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 10 at 5:35PM MST until August 10 at 7:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
At 535 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.8 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
up to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Isidro, Kitt Peak, Fresnal Canyon and Pan Tak.

This includes the following highways...
Route 86 between mile markers 122 and 143. Route 286 between mile
markers 23 and 39.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Altar Wash, Banner Wash, Puertocito Wash, San Juan Wash, Solano
Wash, Alambre Wash, Sabino Wash, Anegan Wash, Fresno Wash, Mulberry
Wash, Cerro Prieto Wash, Sells Wash, Viopuli Wash, Fresnal Wash,
Baboquivari Wash, Ali Molina Wash, Mendoza Wash, South Mendoza
Wash, Topawa Wash, Contreras Wash, Pan Tak Wash, Brawley Wash,
Brown Wash, Saucito Wash, Comobabi Wash, Thomas Canyon Wash and San
Vicente Wash.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.
